tagline: One of the largest independent petroleum refiners in North America
hero_kpi_rationale: Refining throughput (bpd) is the primary operational and financial driver for PBF, as it directly determines petroleum product output and margin generation. Despite the Martinez fire in 2025, this KPI reflects recovery capacity and operational resilience.

kpis.name: Refining throughput
kpis.explanation: Average quantity of crude processed per day across refineries.
kpis.description: PBF's refineries have combined capacity of approximately 1 million barrels per day (bpd), a key indicator of operational scale. This figure is based on current operating conditions.
kpis.signal: Combined capacity stable at 1 million bpd despite incident.

kpis.name: Insurance recovery
kpis.explanation: Amount received from insurance following a loss event.
kpis.description: PBF received $893.5 million in net insurance recoveries in 2025 following the Martinez refinery fire.
kpis.signal: Significant amount received after Martinez fire.

kpis.name: Gain on insurance recovery
kpis.explanation: Accounting gain recognized from insurance payments.
kpis.description: A $832.5 million gain was recognized in the income statement for 2025, net of previously reserved amounts.

kpis.name: Fire-related operating costs
kpis.explanation: Expenses related to managing the Martinez fire.
kpis.description: PBF recorded approximately $163.7 million in operating charges related to the Martinez fire in 2025.
kpis.signal: Significant cost but offset by insurance.

kpis.name: Total revenue
kpis.description: Total revenue extracted from yfinance.income_stmt over four most recent years.
kpis.signal: Total revenue of €29.33 billion in most recent year

kpis.name: Total assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over four most recent years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €13.02 billion in most recent year

kpis.name: Total debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over four most recent years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €2.91 billion in most recent year

kpis.name: Cash and equivalents
kpis.description: Cash and equivalents extracted from yfinance over four most recent years.
kpis.signal: Cash and equivalents of €0.53 billion in most recent year

kpis.name: RBI initiative costs
kpis.explanation: Expenses related to the RBI (internal rationalization) program.
kpis.description: In 2025, PBF launched its RBI initiative and recorded $29.6 million in charges, including $4.7 million in severance costs.
kpis.signal: Launch of an efficiency gains initiative.

kpis.name: Gain on asset sale
kpis.explanation: Gain realized on the sale of refined product terminals.
kpis.description: The sale of two terminals in September 2025 generated a gain of approximately $94 million.

risks.title: Martinez refinery fire
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central in the 10-K, with major operational, financial, and regulatory impacts. Language is strong (ongoing investigations, high costs, insurance dependence). Compared to prior year, this risk is new and dominates 2025 results. The Industrial category carries high weighting in case of total shutdown.

risks.title: Commodity price volatility
risks.score_rationale: Listed as top risk factor, with repeated and emphatic language on crude oil and refined product price volatility. This risk is structural but stable, directly affecting refining margins. The Macro category is systemically critical for refiners.

risks.title: Global geopolitical conflicts
risks.score_rationale: Document explicitly cites Ukraine war, Middle East tensions, and attacks on merchant shipping. Language is alarmist (sanctions, supply chain disruptions). This risk is elevated versus prior year, with strong weighting in context of energy transition.

risks.title: California regulatory pressure
risks.score_rationale: Multiple California laws (AB 32, AB X2-1) cited as risk sources, particularly for Martinez refinery. Language references restrictions on crude extraction and transport. The Regulation category is critical in California, and risk is elevated with local climate agenda.

risks.title: Cyberattacks and technology dependence
risks.score_rationale: Risk is mentioned explicitly, though briefly. Language is generic but reflects increased dependence on digital systems. Stable versus prior year, but Cybersecurity category is increasingly strategic for critical infrastructure.

risks.title: Carbon credit volatility (RINs)
risks.score_rationale: Document emphasizes exposure to RINs and carbon credit markets (AB 32), with price volatility risk. Language is concerned but not alarmist. This risk is stable, but the Competition category includes regulatory costs affecting competitiveness.

risks.title: Debt and financial flexibility
risks.score_rationale: Debt risk addressed multiple times, notably with senior notes issuance in 2025. Language mentions restrictive covenants and rating downgrade risk. Elevated after $800M debt issuance. The Capital category is critical following such refinancing.

ai_positioning.summary: PBF did not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
